USMLE-style practice · Pathology

Toxic impairment of oxygen transport

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

Two adults become confused after operating a fuel-powered generator inside a poorly ventilated garage. Blood gas testing shows a normal arterial oxygen tension, but co-oximetry reveals elevated carboxyhemoglobin. Which change most directly reduces oxygen delivery to their tissues?

  1. Reduced available hemoglobin binding sites and impaired oxygen unloading
  2. Loss of alveolar surfactant as the primary mechanism
  3. Conversion of all hemoglobin iron to the ferric state
  4. Complete destruction of circulating erythrocytes
  5. An isolated fall in plasma dissolved oxygen
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Reduced available hemoglobin binding sites and impaired oxygen unloading

Carbon monoxide occupies hemoglobin and increases oxygen affinity at remaining sites.

Understanding the options

Reduced available hemoglobin binding sites and impaired oxygen unloading
Carbon monoxide occupies hemoglobin and increases oxygen affinity at remaining sites.
Loss of alveolar surfactant as the primary mechanism
Surfactant loss is not the principal mechanism of carbon monoxide poisoning.
Conversion of all hemoglobin iron to the ferric state
Ferric hemoglobin characterizes methemoglobinemia.
Complete destruction of circulating erythrocytes
Hemolysis is not required for carbon monoxide toxicity.
An isolated fall in plasma dissolved oxygen
PaO2 measures dissolved oxygen and may remain normal.
